clue.text: Sick person takes a sort of medicine containing iodine

indicators.note: containing says the medicine word holds the iodine symbol inside it

parts.note: a patent medicine is a proprietary remedy sold over the counter
I is the chemical symbol for iodine

explanation.surface: An invalid is given some proprietary remedy laced with iodine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'containing' puts I inside PATENT; 'takes' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone under medical care is a doctor's patient, so a sick person fits as a direct synonym.

clue.text: Treaty is in the bag, we're told

indicators.note: we're told signals that the phrase before it is heard rather than seen

parts.note: something in the bag has been packed

explanation.surface: A treaty is as good as signed, according to report.
explanation.walkthrough: 'we're told' turns PACKED into its sound-alike; 'In the bag' also means 'certain', which is the surface sense.
explanation.definitionFit: A treaty is a formal agreement between parties, which is what a pact is.

clue.text: Walk most of the way, then take public transport

indicators.note: most of the way says the word is not taken to its end, losing its final letter

parts.note: to tramp is to walk heavily or a long way

explanation.surface: Someone walks nearly all the distance and then hops on a bus or train.
explanation.walkthrough: 'most of the way' drops the last letter P from TRAMP; 'then take' is linking.
explanation.definitionFit: A tram is a street-running passenger vehicle, a form of public transport.

clue.text: Catch fish with broken net first

indicators.note: broken says the letters of net are knocked out of their order

parts.note: to angle is to fish with rod and line

explanation.surface: An angler tries to land fish though their net is torn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broken' rearranges the net, and 'first' puts that ahead of the fish word; 'Catch' looks like a fisherman's verb in the surface, but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To entangle something is to snare or trap it, so it means to catch.

clue.text: Attribute loss of soldiers to fifth columnist

indicators.note: loss of says the soldiers are taken away from the following word

parts.note: a fifth columnist works secretly for the enemy, a betrayer
OR, other ranks, is the usual abbreviation for ordinary soldiers

explanation.surface: A military commander blames the loss of his troops on an enemy sympathiser within.
explanation.walkthrough: 'loss of' takes OR out of TRAITOR. 'Attribute' looks like a verb in the surface but is the noun.
explanation.definitionFit: A trait is a characteristic quality, which is one sense of an attribute.

clue.text: Headline by hack across top of page

indicators.note: across has the cut word lying either side of the letter, enclosing it

parts.note: to hack at something is to slash it

indicators.note: top of picks out the first letter of page

explanation.surface: A journalist writes a front-page headline.
explanation.walkthrough: 'top of' gives P, and 'across' puts SLASH around it; 'Hack' in the surface is a journalist.
explanation.definitionFit: A splash is newspaper jargon for the main front-page story and its big headline.

clue.text: Immediate help for one who's lost for words

definitions.meaning: ... as an adjective means without delay

definitions.text: help for one who's lost for words
definitions.meaning: a cue given to an actor who has forgotten the lines

explanation.surface: An actor who dries on stage gets swift assistance.
explanation.definitionFit: Prompt means instant, and as a noun it is the line fed to a forgetful actor.

clue.text: They are unlikely to take over seats in bar

indicators.note: over signals the letters being turned over into a new order

explanation.surface: Teetotallers are not likely to grab the stools in a pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'take over' looks like one phrase, but 'over' is the anagram signal for SEATS IN BAR; 'take' here means take a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Teetotallers refuse alcohol, so they are the people unlikely to take a drink.

clue.text: Eight-footer came a cropper

definitions.meaning: a long-legged arachnid, which has eight legs
read literally, a farmhand who came to crop the fields at reaping time

explanation.surface: Something with eight legs had a nasty fall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Came a cropper' is British slang for 'fell badly'; here it means a man who came to gather the crop.
explanation.definitionFit: The daddy-longlegs arachnid has this name, and it also names a farm worker at reaping time.

clue.text: Pat's gob spouting rubbish

parts.note: to pat someone on the back is to clap them
gob and trap are both slang for mouth

explanation.surface: Pat's mouth is pouring out nonsense.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pat' looks like a name but is a verb meaning clap; 'spouting' just links to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Claptrap is pretentious nonsense, so it is a synonym for rubbish talk.

clue.text: One to inspire the flower of York? Right!

definitions.text: One to inspire the flower of York? Right!

indicators.note: to inspire is literally to breathe in, so the flower takes a letter inside

parts.note: the white rose is the emblem of the House of York
the pronoun one, as in one never knows, is you, written U

explanation.surface: Someone who stirs up the white rose of Yorkshire, agrees the speaker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to inspire' puts U into ROSE, giving ROUSE, then R follows. The whole clue also describes the answer: a stirring person.
explanation.definitionFit: One who rouses or stirs others to action is a rouser, an inspirer.

clue.text: Boy child features in Bible reading

parts.note: Les is a boy's name, short for Leslie
a son is a male child

explanation.surface: A young boy takes part in reading the scriptures.
explanation.walkthrough: 'features in' is just linking.
explanation.definitionFit: In church a lesson is a passage read aloud from the Bible.

clue.text: House that's in a different location

definitions.meaning: parliamentary jargon by which each House refers to the other chamber

explanation.surface: A home that is situated somewhere else.
explanation.walkthrough: In the UK Parliament the Commons refers to the House of Lords, and vice versa, by this phrase rather than by name.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is Westminster usage for the other chamber, and plainly means elsewhere.

clue.text: Conceited like Gregory, literally

definitions.meaning: the name Gregory has the letters of ego in its centre

explanation.surface: A vain person resembles someone named Gregory.
explanation.walkthrough: Taken literally, the answer says 'ego central': gr-EGO-ry has EGO in its middle.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone self-centred thinks only of themselves, which is being conceited.

clue.text: Bread producer has a profitable business

definitions.meaning: bread is slang for money, so something producing cash
a venture that earns a good return

explanation.surface: A bakery is a lucrative concern.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bread' is slang for money; 'has' is just a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that makes cash brings in money, which is what both senses describe.

clue.text: Piety embraces love to a great extent

indicators.note: embraces says the first word wraps around the second

parts.note: piety is devotion to God, godliness
love means zero in tennis scoring, the letter O

explanation.surface: Religious devotion encompasses a great deal of love.
explanation.walkthrough: 'embraces' puts O inside GODLINESS, after the G; 'to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Goodly can mean considerable in size, so goodliness is largeness or a great extent.

clue.text: Lose to Napoleon? Extremely odd for him!

definitions.text: Lose to Napoleon? Extremely odd for him!

indicators.note: odd says these letters are in a strange order
Extremely takes the first and last letters of Napoleon

explanation.surface: It would be strange for the great admiral to be beaten by the French emperor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Extremely' gives N and N from Napoleon; 'odd' rearranges LOSE plus NN. Nelson beat Napoleon's fleet at Trafalgar, so losing would be odd for him.
explanation.definitionFit: Horatio Nelson was the British admiral who defeated Napoleon's navy, so losing to him would be unlike him.

clue.text: Head teachers

definitions.meaning: the National Union of Teachers, a British teaching union

explanation.surface: A headteacher.
explanation.walkthrough: The National Union of Teachers was the main teaching trade union in England and Wales.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for one's head, and the initials of the National Union of Teachers.

clue.text: Leading hostilities is IDS? Quite the reverse!

parts.note: a star is the leading performer
hostilities are wars

explanation.surface: Is the Tory leader Iain Duncan Smith at the forefront of the fighting?
explanation.walkthrough: IDS was Iain Duncan Smith, then Conservative leader; reversed it is SDI, the Strategic Defense Initiative, nicknamed after the film saga.
explanation.definitionFit: Reagan's Strategic Defense Initiative, SDI, was popularly called by the film title.

clue.text: Tip of tail, shall we say?

indicators.note: shall we say suggests a word spoken rather than spelt

parts.note: a queue is a pigtail, a tail of hair

explanation.surface: Asking about the end of an animal's tail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shall we say' signals a soundalike: QUEUE, a pigtail, sounds like the answer; 'of' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A cue is a hint or signal, which is one sense of a tip.

clue.text: Where to see stars a short time before song on stage

indicators.note: on, in an across clue, says these pieces follow after the next one

parts.note: a plane is a level or stage of development
T is the abbreviation of time, a time cut short
an aria is a solo song in an opera

explanation.surface: A theatre is where you catch celebrities just before they sing.
explanation.walkthrough: In an across clue 'on' means 'after', and 'before' keeps time ahead of song. The stars are in the sky, not celebrities on stage.
explanation.definitionFit: Planetariums project the night sky on a dome, so they are where stars are seen.

clue.text: Little boy with current issue of "The Inventor"

parts.note: Ed is short for Edward, a diminutive
I is the symbol for electric current
issue means offspring, such as a son

explanation.surface: A youngster with the latest copy of a magazine called The Inventor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'issue' looks like a magazine number but means offspring; 'with' and 'of' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: Thomas Edison, inventor of the phonograph, is often called simply the great inventor.

clue.text: Boasters such as Tony Benn?

definitions.meaning: people who boast of famous acquaintances
Benn renounced his title and pared his name down to plain Tony Benn

explanation.surface: Show-offs like the Labour politician Tony Benn.
explanation.walkthrough: Tony Benn, a Labour politician, disclaimed his peerage as Viscount Stansgate and dropped the grand name Anthony Wedgwood Benn.
explanation.definitionFit: People who casually mention famous friends to impress are boasters of a kind.

clue.text: Nose left to do a bit of snooping

definitions.text: to do a bit of snooping

parts.note: the prow is the nose of a ship

explanation.surface: A nosy person is left to pry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nose' suggests nosiness, but is the front of a boat.
explanation.definitionFit: To prowl is to move stealthily looking around, a form of snooping.

clue.text: Criticise elevation of perjurer

indicators.note: elevation in a down clue means the word is raised, read from bottom to top

parts.note: to rail against something is to criticise it

explanation.surface: Condemning the promotion of someone who lied under oath.
explanation.walkthrough: 'elevation of' reads RAIL upwards in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A perjurer lies under oath, so is a liar.

clue.text: Girl grasping left hand

indicators.note: grasping has the girl holding the letter inside her

parts.note: Pam is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A girl holds her left hand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'grasping' puts L inside PAM.
explanation.definitionFit: The palm is the inner surface of the hand, used here as a part for the whole.

clue.text: Drinks hard, being dissolute

parts.note: raki is an aniseed spirit from Turkey and the Balkans
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: Someone who drinks heavily is leading a debauched life.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hard' looks like an adverb but gives H; 'being' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A rakish person behaves like a rake, a dissolute man about town.

clue.text: A boy with a can starting to make short work of it

parts.note: a son is a boy
a tin is a can

explanation.surface: A lad with a tin can quickly finishes a job.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue's opening A is placed last; 'starting to make' and 'of it' only link. 'Short work' is a short musical work.
explanation.definitionFit: A sonatina is a short, simple sonata, so a short piece of music.

clue.text: Many a love token to show affection

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, many
a ring is given as a token of love

explanation.surface: Giving a lot of love tokens is a way of displaying fondness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Many' giving C uses the Roman numeral 100.
explanation.definitionFit: Caring, as an activity, is showing concern and affection for someone.

clue.text: Had an irrepressible desire to drink for a number of years

parts.note: lust is an overwhelming craving
rum is a spirit, a drink

explanation.surface: Someone longed desperately for a drink over several years.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Had' and 'to' are linking; the number of years is five.
explanation.definitionFit: A lustrum is a period of five years, from the Roman purification ceremony held every five years.
